title: Pandas Series Architecture & Access Simulator
description: Visualize 1D labeled series creation, label-based (.loc) vs positional (.iloc) lookups, vectorized arithmetic, in-place modification, and label alignment.

steps.title: Create 1D Labeled Series in Memory
steps.explanation: Pandas creates a two-column internal structure: the Index mapping semantic strings ('Arun', 'Priya', ...) and the Values array storing the numerical integers [80, 90, 75, 85].

steps.title: Label-Based Access with .loc
steps.explanation: .loc searches the Index column for label string 'Priya'. It retrieves the corresponding entry at that row, returning 90.

steps.title: Position-Based Access with .iloc
steps.explanation: .iloc bypasses custom text labels and uses physical zero-based memory offsets. Offset 0 points to Arun's slot, returning 80.

steps.title: Vectorized Scalar Arithmetic
steps.explanation: Vectorized addition broadcasts scalar +5 across every entry. The index labels remain intact while values become [85, 95, 80, 90].

steps.title: Compute Summary Statistics
steps.explanation: Built-in reduction methods aggregate values across the Series: total sum is 85+95+80+90 = 350, and mean average is 350 / 4 = 87.5.

steps.title: In-Place Label Mutation
steps.explanation: Series objects are mutable. Locating label 'Rahul' in the original series updates its value from 75 to 78 without creating a new object.

steps.title: Automatic Label Alignment
steps.code: s1 = pd.Series([10, 20], index=['A', 'B']); s2 = pd.Series([5, 15], index=['B', 'C']); s1 + s2
steps.explanation: When operating between two Series, Pandas aligns rows by matching index labels: 'B' aligns (20+5=25), while unmatched labels 'A' and 'C' evaluate to NaN.
